title: How to increase a number by a percentage
task: Add a percentage to a value in one step — a 10% raise, a price plus tax, a target bumped up by 15%.
keywords: grow a value by a percent google sheets

excel.note: A2 = the value, B2 = the percent (as 0.1 or a cell formatted 10%). The 1+ keeps the original and adds the increase in one multiply.

google_sheets.note: Identical. For a literal percent: =A2*1.1 adds 10%.

explanation: Multiplying by (1 + rate) grows a number by that rate in a single step: 200 × (1 + 0.1) = 220, i.e. the original 200 plus 10% (20). The key is the 1+, which preserves the starting value — A2*B2 alone would give just the 20 increase, not the new total. Enter the rate as a decimal (0.1) or type 10% into the cell, which Excel and Sheets store as 0.1 automatically. To decrease instead, subtract: =A2*(1-B2) takes 10% off. To find what rate turns one number into another, rearrange to =(new-old)/old (see percentage-change). Chaining increases isn't additive — two 10% rises multiply to 1.1×1.1 = 21% total, not 20%.
